title: Runtime API: request schema, error taxonomy, and compatibility guarantees (draft)
content:
Purpose
This doc proposes a unified request schema for the serving runtime, an accompanying error taxonomy, and a set of compatibility guarantees we will commit to across kernel, model, and deployment changes. It is intended for runtime engineers, client SDK authors, and product teams that depend on stable inference semantics.

Goals
- Define a minimal, extensible request shape that covers: text generation, chat/turn semantics, streaming, and KV-backed prefix caching hooks.
- Enumerate error classes (retryable v non-retryable), mapping to HTTP/gRPC codes and suggested client behavior.
- Specify backward/forward compatibility guarantees and feature negotiation for kernel-level changes (e.g., kv cache layout, quantization modes).
- Surface open questions and a deprecation timeline for breaking changes.

Context and non-goals
- This is not a language-model API redesign; we preserve the existing high-level operations (generate/chat/embeddings). The focus is the wire schema, error semantics, and compatibility rules for the serving runtime.
- Non-goal: perf micro-optimizations (separate docs cover batch scheduling and kernel tuning).

1) Request schema (top-level shape)
We propose a compact JSON envelope for all inference requests. Clients SHOULD use this envelope for both REST and gRPC conversions. Fields marked optional may be omitted; unknown fields must be ignored by servers (forward compatibility).

Top-level fields (required unless noted):
- request_id (string): client-generated RFC4122 UUID recommended. Used for idempotency and tracing.
- operation (string): one of "generate", "chat", "embed", "rerank".
- model (string): model identifier, e.g. "redwood/ascend-7b-v2".
- inputs (string | array): prompt text, or array of messages for chat.
- params (object - optional): tuning knobs (temperature, max_tokens, top_p, stop). Unknown keys tolerated.
- streaming (boolean - optional, default: false): whether client wants streamed partial outputs.
- kv_context (object - optional): hint for KV cache semantics (see below).
- client_metadata (object - optional): freeform metadata (SDK version, app id).

Notes:
- We intentionally do not bake model-specific kernel flags into top-level required fields. Those live in params or in an explicit "engine" extension.
- Servers MUST accept inputs as either a flat string or an array of message objects. Message objects for chat MAY include role and name fields.

KV cache (kv_context) semantics
We need a small surface so clients can opt into prefix reuse and help the runtime decide on caching keys. kv_context fields (all optional):
- prefix_id (string): opaque key representing a cached prefix (client-provided or returned by a prior response). If provided, runtime SHOULD try to re-use prefix KV if compatible.
- prefix_length (int): token count of the prefix. Helps scheduling and routing.
- cache_strategy (string): one of "strict", "best-effort". "strict" => require cache hit or fail; "best-effort" => use cache if compatible otherwise compute.
- cache_signature (string): hash representing tokenization + model variant (used for compatibility checks).

Behavior:
- Servers MUST reject (400 Bad Request) prefix_id when cache_signature mismatch indicates incompatible model/kernel variant unless client specified cache_strategy=best-effort.
- Servers MAY return a prefix_id in responses. Prefix IDs are ephemeral and may be invalidated by upgrades. Clients must treat prefix_id as a hint, not a durable identifier.

2) Response envelope and streaming chunks
Full responses and streaming chunks will use the same envelope with fields:
- request_id (string)
- status (string): "ok" | "partial" | "error"
- event (string - optional): for streaming, values like "token", "delta", "end"
- payload (object | string): result payload. For generation, payload.text or payload.tokens; for embeddings, payload.vector.
- prefix_id (string - optional): when runtime creates/returns a prefix key.
- error_code (string - optional): short symbolic code (see taxonomy).

Streaming specifics:
- Streaming chunks MUST be cumulative (clients may receive a token stream) but servers SHOULD include a sequence number for reordering detection.
- For HTTP/1 streaming we use chunked JSON lines; for HTTP2+/gRPC we use standard streaming frames using the same envelope.

3) Error taxonomy and recommended client behavior
We propose three broad classes: transient, user, and compat. Map to HTTP as guidance. Each error carries an error_code and human_text.

Transient (retryable): temporary resource or infra problems. Backoff recommended.
- HTTP 429 / 503 mapping examples:
  - ERROR_RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED (429): soft rate limit. Retry with backoff and jitter.
  - ERROR_CAPACITY_SHORTAGE (503): no GPU slot available right now; client may retry, optionally target a fallback model.
  - ERROR_BACKEND_OVERLOAD (503): internal queueing overload.

User errors (non-retryable): malformed requests, invalid params.
- HTTP 400 mapping examples:
  - ERROR_INVALID_INPUT: bad JSON or tokenization mismatch (client should fix request).
  - ERROR_TOO_LONG_PROMPT: prompt length exceeds allowed model/context window. Client should truncate or use a model with larger context.

Compatibility / security errors (non-retryable or conditional): semantics around kernel/model incompatibility.
- HTTP 409 mapping examples:
  - ERROR_KV_CACHE_INCOMPATIBLE: provided prefix_id or cache_signature incompatible with current serving kernel/version. If cache_strategy=best-effort, server should fall back instead of 409.
  - ERROR_MODEL_VARIANT_MISMATCH: requested model variant not available on the selected node/region. Client may retry with a different model or omit pinned variant.
  - ERROR_SIGNATURE_REQUIRED: client attempted an operation requiring additional auth or attestation (e.g., HSM-protected key).

Internal/unknown (non-diagnostic): 500. Clients should surface message to user and contact support. Include request_id to help debugging.

Error fields in response:
- error_code (string) - one of canonical codes above
- human_text (string) - short explanation
- retry_after (int - optional) - seconds to wait for retry if applicable
- diagnostic_hint (string - optional) - short machine-readable tag for logs (not user-facing)

Idempotency and retries
- request_id is the primary idempotency key. Servers should treat repeated request_id + same operation+model+inputs as idempotent for a short window (recommendation: 10 minutes).
- For streaming requests, clients must re-issue a fresh request_id for full replays; partial reconnections SHOULD use a resumable token (future work).

4) Compatibility guarantees (runtime promises)
We must be explicit about what we will not break and what we may change with notice.
Must-stay-stable (backwards compatibility):
- Top-level envelope and field names (request_id, operation, model, inputs, params) will be stable across minor kernel and model rollouts.
- Error codes listed above are stable contractual strings; we will not remove or rename them without a deprecation cycle.
- Semantic behavior for idempotency via request_id (10-minute window) will hold.

May-change-with-notice (requires deprecation timeline):
- Internal semantics of prefix_id (format, invalidation policy) are ephemeral. We guarantee only that prefix_id returned by server will work for the serving lifetime indicated by server via headers or explicit TTL in response. We will provide at least 30 days notice before changing prefix semantics that break client-presumed format.
- Kernel-level ABI changes that affect cache_signature meaning: we will publish a migration guide and a compatibility matrix. Breaking kernel ABI changes will be flagged as major and only rolled with customers on Dedicated/Private via a separate ops plan. Hosted customers will be migrated with automated fallback to compatible model variants.

Forward compatibility guarantees (how clients should handle unknown fields):
- Clients MUST ignore unknown response fields.
- Servers MUST ignore unknown request fields.
- Servers SHOULD support new enum values in params as "best-effort" fallback to preserve forward compatibility.

Feature negotiation and capability discovery
We will introduce a lightweight capability endpoint (GET /v1/runtime/capabilities or similar) that returns a list of runtime features, supported params, and kernel version string. Fields: supported_models, kv_cache_modes, streaming_formats, max_context_tokens, kernel_version. Clients MUST use this endpoint to adapt behavior when connecting to a new region or Dedicated/private deployment.

Deprecation and versioning policy
- We will follow semver-like major/minor model at the API surface level. Major changes (breaking) require a migration window of >= 90 days and explicit customer notices; minor (additive) changes are communicated in release notes.
- Broken behaviors fixed in minor releases must be non-breaking to clients that follow the rules (ignore unknown fields, use explicit params).

Operational notes for runtime implementers
- The runtime should perform cache_signature checks early in the request pipeline to fail fast and minimize wasted scheduler cycles.
- When detecting KV incompatibility, prefer to return ERROR_KV_CACHE_INCOMPATIBLE with suggested remediation (e.g., drop prefix_id or set cache_strategy=best-effort).
- Log request_id, kernel_version, model_variant, and node_id for every failed request to help debugging.

Open questions / TODOs
- Resumable streaming: design a resumable token and semantics for reconnecting to an in-progress stream. (JIRA-RT-93)
- Exact TTL semantics for prefix_id and whether TTL should be declaratively returned in every response.
- Should cache_signature be a client-computable hash (based on tokenizer+model_version) or runtime-assigned? Tradeoffs for privacy and load.
- Groom a canonical list of error_code strings and map to gRPC codes for SDKs.

Appendix: example request/response
Example (non-streaming generation):
{
  "request_id": "c18f6b7a-1f4a-4d5b-9e9a-0f9b7a2b4c3d",
  "operation": "generate",
  "model": "redwood/ascend-7b-v2",
  "inputs": "Write a one-paragraph summary of the file below.",
  "params": { "temperature": 0.2, "max_tokens": 256 },
  "kv_context": { "prefix_id": "pfx-9a1b-xxx", "cache_strategy": "best-effort", "cache_signature": "tok-v1:ascend-7b-v2:sha256:..." }
}

Server OK response:
{
  "request_id": "c18f6b7a-1f4a-4d5b-9e9a-0f9b7a2b4c3d",
  "status": "ok",
  "payload": { "text": "Summary paragraph..." },
  "prefix_id": "pfx-xyz-20250220"
}

Server incompatible cache response (client used strict):
{
  "request_id": "...",
  "status": "error",
  "error_code": "ERROR_KV_CACHE_INCOMPATIBLE",
  "human_text": "Provided prefix_id is incompatible with current model variant. Retry without prefix or set cache_strategy=best-effort."
}

Contact
Ping eng-serving-runtime on Slack or open PR against the serving-runtime repo. Major changes to the envelope must be coordinated with SDK owners (developer-experience) and product.

Revision history

- 2025-02-20 A. Kumar edits: error taxonomy expanded, added capability discovery note
